events.title: Buttonwood Agreement Signed
events.description: Twenty-four stockbrokers and merchants signed the Buttonwood Agreement under a buttonwood tree outside 68 Wall Street in New York City, establishing rules for trading securities and setting commission rates.
events.significance: This agreement is considered the founding of what later became the New York Stock Exchange, which grew into the largest stock exchange in the world.

events.title: Brown v. Board of Education Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court unanimously ruled in Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional, declaring that separate educational facilities are inherently unequal.
events.significance: The decision overturned the doctrine of separate but equal from Plessy v. Ferguson in public education and became a catalyst for the American civil rights movement.

events.title: World Health Organization Removes Homosexuality from Disease Classification
events.description: The World Health Organization's World Health Assembly endorsed the 10th revision of the International Classification of Diseases, which removed homosexuality from its list of mental disorders.
events.significance: The date is now observed annually as the International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia, marking a milestone in global LGBTQ+ rights and medical recognition.

events.title: Norwegian Constitution Signed
events.description: Norway's constitution was signed at Eidsvoll on May 16 and formally dated and proclaimed on May 17, when the Constituent Assembly elected Christian Frederik as king, declaring Norway an independent kingdom after the separation from Denmark.
events.significance: May 17 is celebrated as Norway's Constitution Day, the country's national day, commemorating its independence and one of Europe's most liberal constitutions of the era.
